narrator.instruct: Fast-paced, energetic, punchy explainer narrator. Brisk delivery with no long pauses.

owner.instruct: Sly, cheerful shop owner letting you in on a secret, quick and smug.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You just grabbed a jacket for forty-nine ninety-nine. Basically forty bucks.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You feel smart. You even skipped the one that cost fifty.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At the register you pay, grab your bag, and grin all the way out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Then the back door swings open. The owner is re-tagging every price with a little gun.

lines.speaker: owner
lines.text: One cent off. Works every single time.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That cent was never a discount. It was aimed at your eyes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: We read prices left to right, and the first digit hits hardest.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In two thousand five, researchers showed why two ninety-nine feels smaller than three dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One cent changes the left digit, and your brain stops reading there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A clothing catalog tested the same dress at forty-four, forty-nine and fifty-four dollars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At forty-four and fifty-four, sales were almost the same.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: At forty-nine, the dress sold clearly more.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Economists checked over twenty-two million used car sales at auction.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Each time the odometer rolled past another ten thousand miles, prices dropped.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: That's about one hundred fifty to two hundred dollars, for a single mile.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: So the nine isn't there for your wallet. It's there for your eyes.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Next door, a sign says nine ninety-nine, and you're already reaching for your card.
